executiveSummary: GM1724 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 59 neighbourhoods, four BAG places, 26 BRT settlements, four NWB links, null semantics, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and sustained-water repair guard are coherent. Release remains correction-required for three spatial-evidence defects. First, the named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns Bergeijk sustained direct municipality-wide inundation stress even though the official Brabant-Zuidoost profile places the region outside direct large-river influence and the municipality identifies a different system of small, partly Belgian-fed catchments. Internal inundation stress reaches 2.076244 at T+12, persists through T+72, and produces 8,709 modeled people under pressure and 740,596 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours at T+72. Second, river and pluvial neighbourhood maps inherit the same seeded order rather than the municipality's documented rainwater locations, streams and terrain. Third, a focused synthetic wildfire placed inside De Pielis makes its containing neighbourhood rank only eleventh while a neighbourhood almost eight kilometres from the source ranks first, because local allocation ignores source geometry. The public layer usefully exposes 114 water objects and provider responsibility, but neither causally changes the simulation. All utility views honestly label their shared N69/N397 road flows logical transfer proxies. Physical Brabant Water, Enexis, sewer, telecom, facility and emergency-supply topology, Belgian lifelines, live state, backup, stocks, crews and restoration estimates remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, definitief versie 1.0
supports: Bergeijk is one of the 21 municipalities in Brabant-Zuidoost. The profile explicitly places the region outside direct influence of sea and large-river flooding while retaining high-water and defence risks along smaller rivers such as the Dommel and Aa and risks from extreme rain.

The cross-border assessment identifies a Pelt high-water retention basin, large Belgian-Dutch forest/heath complexes, possible Belgian-origin nature fire, and the N69 as a hazardous-material corridor.

The all-hazard analysis covers high water, extreme rain, dike breach, wildfire, winter weather, heat, storm, loss of electricity, gas, telecom, drinking water and wastewater treatment, and cyberattack; it also records cascading dependencies among vital processes.

Waterschappen De Dommel and Aa en Maas, Enexis, KPN, Brabant Water and Rijkswaterstaat contributed, supporting provider/dependency relevance but not any exact GM1724 topology, capacity, inventory or restoration value.
The profile is a strategic four-year publication, not a live warning, probability feed or machine-readable event footprint; no explicit dataset reuse licence is stated in the PDF.

evidenceSources.title: Verbreed Gemeentelijk Rioleringsplan 2025–2029
supports: Official local inventory distinguishes 117 km mixed, 22 km wastewater, 27 km rainwater, 2 km drainage and 7 km infiltration/transport sewer; 8,600 gullies; 36 km pressure main and 47 km pressure sewer; 35 main pumping stations including overflow facilities and 226 mini-pump units; 5 ha wadis/soil passages; 314 km watercourses; 93 culverts; 26 external overflow/other facilities; and 60 rain/groundwater/sewer measurement points.

Only main pumps and overflow facilities have telemetry; the 226 mini-pumps do not. The municipality says its internal asset view is current and inspection-based, but it is not exposed as a licensed live public operations API.

The 2018 municipal climate stress test was a first global impression and the plan says it should be updated on the usual six-year cycle, so it is authoritative context rather than current incident observation.
The publication is machine-readable as official HTML/XML/ODT/PDF and is a five-year policy/inventory source; no explicit GIS redistribution licence or live update cadence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Het groene karakter (tussen bossen, beken en boerenland) — water and climate adaptation
supports: Official local context distinguishes Beerze, Dommel and Belgian Nete subcatchments; Aa/Goorloop, Dalemstroompje, Run, Rijtjes, Beekloop and Keersop; and multiple tributaries whose headwaters partly originate in Belgium.
The municipality names parts of Bergeijk ('t Loo and 't Hof), Luyksgestel, Weebosch and the countryside as rainwater-vulnerable and identifies groundwater concern along Keersop and Run.
Heat varies with vegetation and paving; half the municipal vegetation is drought-sensitive. Extensive forest complexes occur on the dry south-western and south-eastern cover sands.

The page reports place-based flood probability and fatality risk as zero and a scenario depth range of 0–0.5 m, reinforcing that its planning products must not be replaced by a generic main-river scalar.
This is current authoritative policy/context with embedded presentation maps, not a stable machine GIS service or live hazard feed; update cadence and reuse licence are not stated.

evidenceSources.title: Stap vooruit in beheersing natuurbranden in De Kempen
supports: Bergeijk, Eersel, Bladel, Reusel-De Mierden, VRBZO and Staatsbosbeheer signed a De Kempen wildfire-management plan and committed to an implementation plan.

Named prevention actions include replacing conifers with deciduous trees, wetting nature areas and improving emergency-service access, establishing that fuel type, moisture and access are locally material.

This is authoritative current response/context evidence, not a machine incident perimeter, fuel/moisture surface, suppression-resource feed or first-72-hour spread model; no fixed cadence or reuse licence is stated.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The generic major-river field and shared seeded neighbourhood ordering do not represent Bergeijk's streams, catchments, rainwater locations, forests or explicit event source.
notes: River stress rises from zero at T+0 to 0.730838 at T+6 and 2.076244 at T+12, remaining 2.076244 through T+72; affected population is 6,210 at T+12, 7,859 at T+24 and 8,709 at T+48/T+72.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-460 derives river exposure from municipality-centre distance to three coarse diagonal segments; lines 617-622 apply a scalar without a selected connected river/catchment footprint, water level, defence, arrival or duration layer.
E03 explicitly excludes direct large-river influence and E05 identifies different Dommel, Beerze and Nete pathways; none causes the generic municipality-wide result.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3351-3365 applies municipality severity multiplied by a shared deterministic regional seed. River and pluvial therefore have the identical exact ranking across all 59 neighbourhoods.

At pluvial T+24 district mean severity ranks Westerhoven first, Riethoven second, Buitengebied third, Bergeijk 't Hof fourth, Luyksgestel fifth, Bergeijk 't Loo sixth and Weebosch seventh. E05 names parts of 't Loo, 't Hof, Luyksgestel and Weebosch as vulnerable; the model neither ingests nor validates against that analysis.

In a focused synthetic T+24 wildfire with source [5.2527, 51.2842] inside BRT De Pielis and CBS BU17240608 Buitengebied Zuid-West, that containing neighbourhood ranks 11/59 at 0.486836 while BU17240004 Burgemeester Magneestraat ranks first at 0.521587. The respective neighbourhood centres are about 1.305 km and 7.984 km from the source. This diagnostic proves local allocation ignores the selected source; it is not an observed fire or claim about current conditions.
Coastal direct inundation remains exactly zero, correctly separating no local coastal water from the preset's wind-only indirect service stress.

notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.

notes: River forcing remains active at T+72, all eight service recovery-progress values remain exactly zero, pressure is 0.460880, 8,709 people remain under pressure and cumulative proxy burden reaches 740,596 person-hours.

Actual drainage, provider switching, forest access, roads, Belgian assistance, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staffing, stock and restoration estimates are unknown.

findings.summary: A coarse proximity corridor creates unsupported sustained direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation across Bergeijk.
findings.evidence: E03 explicitly places Brabant-Zuidoost outside direct large-river influence while retaining smaller-river, extreme-rain and defence mechanisms; E05 distinguishes Beerze, Dommel and Nete subcatchments and reports place-based flood probability/fatality risk as zero with a 0–0.5 m planning depth range. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-460 nevertheless measures the GM1724 centroid against three coarse diagonal segments, and lines 617-622 turn that screen into direct water. The canonical named-major-river frame emits internal inundation stress 0.730838 at T+6 and 2.076244 at T+12 through T+72, with 7,859 modeled people/186,622 event-attributable service person-hours at T+24 and 8,709 people/740,596 person-hours at T+72. All restoration remains zero because the synthetic water persists. No selected connected scenario, defence, water level, arrival, duration or locally valid depth supports that result. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared national proximity-field defect, not a claim that Bergeijk lacks local high-water or rain risk.
findings.action: Mark GM1724's current direct named-major-river result unsupported/Unknown and numerically neutral in downstream decisions until an expert-selected source footprint exists; preserve Dommel/Beerze/Nete, groundwater, regional-defence and pluvial mechanisms as unresolved rather than safe. The durable fix must intersect a named/versioned LIWO or water-board scenario and expose people/services only within an approved connected footprint.

findings.summary: One seeded neighbourhood order replaces Bergeijk's documented mechanism-specific rainwater locations, streams and terrain.
findings.evidence: E05 names parts of 't Loo, 't Hof, Luyksgestel and Weebosch as rainwater-vulnerable and groundwater concern along Keersop and Run; E04 requires a catchment-aware approach and says the 2018 stress test was global and due for update. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3351-3365 instead applies one hazardSeed multiplier to municipality severity. River and pluvial therefore have an identical exact 59-neighbourhood order, starting with Burgemeester Magneestraat, Kapellerweg-Rijt and Eviestraat-Vlasstraat. At pluvial T+24 the district mean puts 't Loo sixth and Weebosch seventh, while the model ingests no stress-test cell, surface, stream, sewer or elevation. The ranking is reproducible synthetic allocation, not validation against the official local locations.
findings.action: Mark neighbourhood direct-water distribution unsupported until a versioned source layer is supplied. Obtain the municipality's updated climate-stress-test GIS and/or Klimaateffectatlas water-depth grids, preserve event/return period, cell size, unit, edition, no-data and uncertainty, and use AHN/IMWA/GWSW only as disclosed covariates. Add fixtures proving river and pluvial footprints can differ and approved source cells—not a hash—govern local direct impact.

findings.summary: An explicit De Pielis wildfire source does not control the neighbourhood map shown for direct local impact.
findings.evidence: E03/E06 establish major cross-border forest/heath fire relevance and locally material vegetation, wetting and emergency-access factors. The canonical remote wildfire coherently yields zero direct flame at Bergeijk, so a focused synthetic scenario placed the source at [5.2527, 51.2842] inside BRT De Pielis and CBS BU17240608 Buitengebied Zuid-West. At T+24 the municipality has direct-fire intensity 0.385079, smoke 0.540430 and severity 0.447130, but the containing neighbourhood ranks only 11/59 at 0.486836; BU17240004 Burgemeester Magneestraat ranks first at 0.521587 despite its centre being 7.984 km from the source versus 1.305 km for the containing area. The order is the same shared seed seen for water because packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3351-3365 never uses local source distance or intersection. This is a synthetic reproducibility test, not evidence of an observed/current fire.
findings.action: Until polygon-aware local fire allocation exists, label municipality and neighbourhood flame footprints synthetic/unsupported and do not use their rank for deployment. Prefer an authorized NIPV Risiko-index Natuurbranden export; otherwise combine BRT TOP10NL land cover, timestamped KNMI weather/fuel-moisture proxies and an explicit source/perimeter with visibly scenario-based spread assumptions. Tests must prioritize source-intersecting cells and make wind/fuel/access inputs inspectable.

findings.summary: The public water layer is useful context but far too incomplete and non-causal for first-72-hour drainage performance.
findings.evidence: E08 contributes 111 weirs and three sewer pumps within the generalized boundary. E04 separately inventories 35 main pumps including overflow facilities plus 226 mini-pump units, 166 km of gravity sewer, 83 km of pressure/force main, 314 km watercourses, 93 culverts and monitoring distinctions. These scopes cannot be reconciled as a complete public network, and the application correctly marks public assets affectsSimulation=false. Pluvial T+24 drainage availability 0.613344 and its T+48/T+72 recovery therefore come from generic equations, not connectivity, pump/overflow state, telemetry, storage, downstream RWZI Eindhoven, emergency power or observed maintenance.
findings.action: Retain IMWA/DAMO/GWSW objects as partial non-causal context. Request a licensed, security-reviewed municipal GWSW/hydraulic topology and exercise state; only then add catchment-to-pump/storage/downstream dependencies. Where data cannot be released, offer a bounded named drainage-subsystem scenario with explicit pump/telemetry/backup assumptions rather than inferring function from public points.

findings.summary: Dutch-only corridors omit Bergeijk's Belgian water, fire, mobility and response dependencies.
findings.evidence: E03 identifies the Pelt retention basin, Belgian-origin nature-fire paths and N69 as cross-border risk context; E05 says part of De Pielis drains to the Belgian Nete and multiple headwaters partly originate in Belgium. The generated network has four N69/N397 routes to Valkenswaard, Veldhoven and Eersel and zero foreign endpoints. It cannot represent N69/N74 continuity, Belgian emergency access, supply or water governance. Applying all four road corridors unchanged to power, water, drainage, gas and telecom would be especially misleading even though transferSemantics is correctly logical-proxy.
findings.action: Add explicit, service-eligible Belgian boundary gateways only after authoritative Dutch/Flemish road, water and mutual-aid review. Keep unknown capacity editable, delayed and scenario-labeled; never clone a foreign road gateway into a physical utility edge. Preserve catchment direction/authority separately from mobility, facilities and supply.

findings.summary: Provider territory is known, but physical utility state, topology, capacity and restoration are not publicly established.
findings.evidence: The live public Stichting Mijn Aansluiting lookup at the municipality reference point returned Enexis for electricity/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed media; drainage returned no polygon. E03 supports those provider/dependency categories but no exact service numbers. Provider areas and Enexis public static asset extracts can identify responsibility/context only, not loading, pressure, switching, failure, backup, priority customers, crews or restoration. All current availability/demand/delivery values remain transparent synthetic scenario outputs.
findings.action: Keep provider areas affectsSimulation=false and expose per-discipline coverage/timestamp. Integrate authorized operator exercise data when available; otherwise retain service-specific bounded priors, sensitivity controls and explicit Unknown operational state. Do not turn current connection-capacity congestion or a static asset record into outage likelihood.

findings.summary: Weather, cyber and earthquake presets are scenario exercises rather than Bergeijk observations or local probability estimates.
findings.evidence: E03 supports storm, heat, winter, nature fire, high-water, vital-service and cyber scenarios and also identifies natural-earthquake possibility in Limburg/Noord-Brabant. The canonical earthquake instead has a Groningen epicentre and only 0.004217 peak severity at Bergeijk; cyber forcing is a configured target process; weather values are generated envelopes. No KNMI warning, station/nowcast, earthquake record, operator incident or local calibration drives these frames. The ten-preset contract also omits nearby cross-border radiological and hazardous-material risks documented by E03.
findings.action: Keep all presets clearly labeled synthetic. For live/context mode, ingest timestamped KNMI Open Data observations/forecasts and the KNMI earthquake catalogue with dataset licence/validity retained; require a selected epicentre and ground-motion model for earthquake. Keep cyber and omitted risk types as explicit exercise inputs until authorized incident/scenario evidence exists.

findings.summary: Direct coastal water and canonical remote wildfire flame are zero without falsely erasing indirect or unresolved local risk.
findings.evidence: The coastal preset returns exactly zero direct water/severity at T+24 while its 17.369158 m/s wind component produces bounded indirect service pressure. The canonical wildfire's remote named source returns direct flame zero but separately exposes smoke 0.253602 and drought 0.643250 at T+24. These are scoped event results, not declarations that Bergeijk has no coastal supply dependency or local wildfire risk; GM1724-FIRE-SPAT-001 separately demonstrates the unresolved local allocation.
findings.action: Retain exact direct-zero semantics and the direct/indirect separation. Keep evidence scope visible and never translate a remote preset's zero flame into an all-hazards all-clear.

findings.summary: Identity, demography, boundary, neighbourhood, place, settlement and public-asset provenance are inspectable and null-safe.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 match GM1724, Bergeijk, 19,263 residents, density 191, age-65-plus 4,743 and one-person households 2,533. All 59 neighbourhoods, four BAG places and 26 BRT settlements resolve; 28-person neighbourhood rounding difference is disclosed. Missing district heat/public charging and other suppressed cells remain null. E08 objects retain source/type/status/timestamp fields and affectsSimulation=false.
findings.action: Retain edition, retrieval, licence, coverage and null semantics; refresh annually or at source cadence and rerun the focused/national gates after each snapshot.

findings.summary: The full deterministic, causal and layer-invariance contract passes for Bergeijk.
findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; zero-intensity output is exact zero; local compound T+24 population/affected/service balances reconcile; ledgers close; person-hours are matched no-event essential-service pressure; all eleven layer selections preserve simulation state; and every route says logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic or exact-zero behavior to hide calibration gaps.

corrections.summary: Replace seeded Bergeijk water allocation with source-specific stress-test, terrain, catchment and hydraulic evidence.
corrections.validation: Request the machine GIS behind the municipality's updated climate stress test; its stated six-year planning cadence, precise event/return period, grid resolution, units, edition, no-data, uncertainty and licence must be recorded. The national Klimaateffectatlas download/WMS documented at https://www.klimaateffectatlas.nl/en/faq offers GeoTIFF/GeoPackage/WMS layers under CC BY 4.0 and is updated several times per year; resolution is map-specific and can be approximately 2 m, and the atlas warns it is indicative rather than a local decision model. AHN WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/actueel-hoogtebestand-nederland/wcs/v1_0?SERVICE=WCS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities provides Rijkswaterstaat/PDOK DTM/DSM products at 0.5 m, cyclical AHN editions and CC0. E08 IMWA/DAMO and GWSW OGC https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/waterschappen-waterketen-gwsw/ogc/v1 are disclosed covariates only. Tests must make approved source cells govern local water, preserve no-data as Unknown and permit river/pluvial rankings to differ.

corrections.summary: Make explicit Bergeijk wildfire scenarios polygon/source-aware while preserving unavailable operational resource data as Unknown.
corrections.validation: Preferred source is NIPV's Risiko-index Natuurbranden at https://nipv.nl/informatievoorziening/voorzieningen/risico-index-natuurbranden/: a professional 1 km² multi-parameter risk product. No public documented bulk API, redistribution licence or fixed refresh cadence was found, so request an authorized export and terms rather than scraping the application. Public fallback: Kadaster BRT TOP10NL OGC https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1 provides national 1:10,000 land-cover/terrain under CC BY 4.0 with normally annual releases, combined with a timestamped KNMI dataset whose own metadata, licence and validity are retained. Static land cover is not live fuel moisture or spread. Tests must make the source-intersecting neighbourhood rank above a distant town cell under otherwise equal assumptions, distinguish flame from smoke/drought, and display fuel/wind/access/suppression assumptions.

corrections.summary: Add partial drainage/provider and Belgian-gateway context without inventing physical utility topology or emergency capacity.
corrections.validation: E08 Kunstwerken IMWA/Waterketen DAMO are machine OGC features under CC BY-SA 4.0; Kunstwerken declares weekly updates, has variable contributor completeness and yields 114 intersecting points, so retain retrieval/object timestamps and affectsSimulation=false. GWSW OGC can add CC0 sewer context, while the authoritative E04 municipal inventory/topology requires a licensed security review; absent pump state, connectivity, backup and capacity remain explicit Unknown. Stichting Mijn Aansluiting documents public OGC WMS/WFS provider areas at https://wiki.service.mijnaansluiting.nl/wiki/spaces/Wiki/pages/693731329; retain provider-supplied timestamps and non-causal responsibility semantics. Enexis Asset Data at https://data.overheid.nl/dataset/enexis-assetdata is CC0 static asset context whose catalogue metadata was last updated 2023-01-31 with no periodic cadence. E07 NWB is monthly CC0 Dutch road geometry. For Belgium, evaluate Digitaal Vlaanderen's authoritative Wegenregister machine service and explicit Dutch-Belgian mutual-aid/catchment agreements, recording service licence, snapshot and update cadence before use; if unavailable, a boundary gateway may affect only named mobility/facility/supply exercises after a configurable delay, never power/water/gas/telecom topology.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved Bergeijk LIWO/water-board depth, arrival, duration, defence, small-river, runoff or catchment grid is ingested; internal inundation stress is not measured local metres.

Marking unsupported Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing Unknown must not erase actual Dommel, Beerze, Nete, Keersop, Run, Beekloop, Pelt retention-basin, regional-defence, groundwater, sewer-overload or extreme-rain mechanisms.

The municipal 2018 climate stress test is described as a global planning impression and due for six-year-cycle update; its embedded presentation map is not a licensed native machine surface or live event model.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, forests, fuels, streams, culverts, wadis, sewers, pumps, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.

The public Waterschapshuis layer is intentionally partial; 114 intersecting points cannot be interpreted as Bergeijk's complete 166 km sewer/261-pump/314 km watercourse system or as operational state.

Provider polygons identify responsibility at one reference point, not full physical coverage, topology or state; drainage may be missing and fixed-media provider areas do not represent mobile coverage.

No physical Brabant Water, Enexis, wastewater, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, current state, backup, priority-customer list, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
The Dutch-only graph omits Belgian access, headwaters, agencies, care, suppliers and mutual aid; no operational cross-border agreement or capacity was inferred.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish live closure, timetable/vehicle operation, congestion, evacuation throughput or repair access; no railway station lies inside GM1724.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, acceptance, care-home occupancy, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, current fuel/moisture condition, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the focused De Pielis case is explicitly synthetic.
Earthquake lacks a selected local natural event, ground-motion surface, site response and asset fragility; the canonical Groningen event does not test local earthquake response.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Bergeijk resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, flash runoff, dispatch and restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit radiological, hazardous-material, pipeline and other cross-border risks identified by E03.
